findings.title: Windows identity discovery command executed
findings.consumer_text: A command was executed to identify the current Windows user. This may be normal activity or part of an attempt to gather information about the computer.
findings.false_positive_note: Administrators, troubleshooting scripts, and legitimate software may use whoami.exe during normal operations.
next_steps: Identify the user who executed the command.
Review the parent process and command line.
Check for related unusual discovery commands.
Determine whether the activity was expected.
findings.analyst_notes: Review Sysmon Event ID 1. Examine Image, CommandLine, ParentImage, User, and ProcessGuid. Correlate with other discovery commands and suspicious process activity.

findings.title: PowerShell launched with encoded command
findings.consumer_text: PowerShell was launched on this computer. The command may require investigation because encoded commands can hide what a script is doing.
findings.false_positive_note: Administrators and legitimate automation tools may use encoded PowerShell commands.
next_steps: Review the PowerShell command line.
Decode any encoded command safely for analysis.
Identify the parent process that launched PowerShell.
Determine whether the execution was authorized.
findings.analyst_notes: Review Sysmon Event ID 1. Examine Image, CommandLine, ParentImage, ParentCommandLine, and ProcessGuid. Identify encoded command arguments and correlate related parent-child process activity.

findings.title: Registry Run key modified
findings.consumer_text: A Windows Registry setting used to automatically start programs was modified. This could allow a program to run whenever a user signs in.
findings.false_positive_note: Legitimate applications frequently modify Run keys during installation, updates, or configuration changes.
next_steps: Identify the modified Registry value.
Check which executable or script was configured.
Verify whether the change was authorized.
Investigate unexpected startup programs.
findings.analyst_notes: Review Sysmon Event ID 13 and examine TargetObject, Details, Image, and ProcessGuid. Identify changes to Run and RunOnce keys and correlate with process creation events.
